To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

resonant-tunnel structures based on graphene can have very large conductance, that the conductance is sensitive to the widths and heights of the barriers (or wells), and that the conductance oscillates with the separation between the barriers (or the wells).
resonant tunneling through graphene-based structures is possible and that the resonant transmission features are very sensitive to the structure geometry.
the resonant-tunnel conductance of graphene-based double-barrier structures can be controlled by varying the width and height (depth) of the barriers and the separation between the two barriers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic transport properties of graphene-based resonant-tunnelling structures.
the development of a new generation of nanostructured electronic devices based on the use of graphene.
electronic properties of nano-structures, such as quantum wells, superlattices, and heterostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
graphene-based resonant-tunnelling devices are a promising candidate for the realization of high-speed and low-power electronic devices.
the graphene-based double barrier (well) structures are very promising candidates for the design of future nanoscale electronic devices.
graphene is an excellent candidate for the fabrication of nanoelectronic devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the resonant tunneling through double-barrier structures is a powerful technique for studying electron transport in graphene and for manipulating its electronic properties.
the transmission probability of the double barriers can be enhanced or suppressed by adjusting the widths and heights of the barriers.
the conductance of a graphene-based resonant-tunnelling structure is determined by the transmission probability of the resonant state in the well (hole state in the barrier).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resonant-tunnel transmission through graphene-based structures is very different from the transmission through similar structures made of other two-dimensional semiconductors.
resonant transmission can occur even if the incident wave vector does not coincide with the wave vector of the resonant state.
resonant tunneling through graphene-based structures can be controlled by the wave vector of the incident electron and the geometry of the structure.
